issues.description: Method parameter order mismatch for addChild: The problem statement and the template declare the service method as addChild(Person person, Person child) (parent/target person first, child second). In the solution implementation the method is declared with the parameters swapped: addChild(Person child, Person person). Because both parameters share the same type (Person) this still compiles, but calls written according to the template/problem (e.g., personService.addChild(person, child) in PersonResource) will bind arguments to the wrong parameters and cause the implementation to operate on the wrong object (reversing the intended parent/child roles). This discrepancy between template/problem and solution is likely to confuse students and produce incorrect runtime behavior if the solution's signature is used as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's addChild method signature match the problem statement and template: declare it as addChild(Person person, Person child). Update the parameter names and the method body accordingly (use child.getParents() checks and add child to person's children: person.getChildren().add(child); then save 'person'). Alternatively, if keeping the swapped parameter order is deliberate, update all call sites (PersonResource and tests) and the problem statement/template consistently to use the same parameter order. The recommended fix for minimal confusion is to use addChild(Person person, Person child) in the solution and adjust its implementation.
